resources.string: How to use QuicMic
How to use this app
What this app does

QuicMic turns your phone into a wireless microphone for your PC. You talk into the phone, and the PC hears it as a mic input — for Discord, games, calls, or recording. Everything stays on your home WiFi: no cloud, no account.
Step 1 — set up the PC

On your PC, run quicmic-windows-x86_64.exe. A window opens showing a big QR code and a 6-digit PIN.

When Windows Firewall asks, allow it on private networks — this is the most common reason pairing fails.

For apps like Discord to hear you, the PC needs a virtual audio device (such as VB-Cable) installed: the app plays your phone’s audio into it, and Discord listens to that device.
Step 2 — pair your phone

Tap \u201cScan QR code\u201d and scan the code in the PC window. It fills in the address and PIN automatically, then tap \u201cFetch server identity\u201d and \u201cConfirm & Pair\u201d.\n\nNo camera? Type the details manually: the PC\u2019s address (looks like 192.168.x.x — find it with ipconfig on the PC), port 8443, and the 6-digit PIN from the PC window.
Same WiFi, always
Both devices must be on the same WiFi network. If your phone is on mobile data (or a guest network), it will never find the PC.
QR shows a weird address?

If the QR code fills in something odd like 10.2.0.2 instead of 192.168.x.x, the PC picked the wrong network (a VPN or virtual adapter). Newer PC versions fix this automatically.\n\nWorkaround: close the PC app, open cmd in its folder, and start it with quicmic-windows-x86_64.exe --ip 192.168.x.x using the PC\u2019s real address from ipconfig. Then scan the fresh QR code.
PIN stopped working?
The PIN can change (for example after a PC restart). If pairing suddenly fails, look at the PC window and use the PIN it shows right now.
Tour of Settings
Audio (mic \u2192 PC): your microphone \u2014 noise gate, gain, echo cancellation, latency recovery, and the phone mic picker.
Speaker (PC \u2192 phone): listen to the PC\u2019s audio on your phone \u2014 volume, delay, output device, and a test tone.
Drop \u2014 file sharing: send files and text between phone and PC, and receive files even with the app in the background.
System: app theme (dark/light), PC update checks, mic naming, and the diagnostics screen.
Quick troubleshooting
\u201cCould not verify server\u201d / timeout: the phone can\u2019t reach the PC. Check \u2014 same WiFi? PC app running? Firewall allowed? Right address?
Choppy or delayed audio: WiFi congestion. Move closer to the router, and try the latency-recovery slider in Audio settings.
Silent after a phone call: the OS took the microphone. Go back to the app and reconnect.
